assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics, with electrons and nuclei propagated together, turned simulation from force-field fitting into a first-principles tool for liquids, interfaces, reactive chemistry and biomolecular active sites (QM/MM). A clear, original idea with a simple formulation and decades of demonstrated consequences; it fits the standard of a game-changer that has already shown real impact.
assessment.attribution: Two-person 1985 paper; the credit is unusually clean and fits a prize of at most three. No other credited name competes for the central idea.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent use and extensions; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue. The 2013 multiscale prize rewarded neighbouring ideas but not this one.
uncertainties: Parrinello also appears in metadynamics and machine-learned potentials; a prize could be framed around him more broadly, which would change the configuration.
Whether the committee views simulation methods as already honoured by 2013 is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity and targeted degradation is a genuinely new drug modality, with PROTACs and molecular glues now in clinical trials. It is a chemical concept (a bifunctional molecule hijacking ubiquitin ligases) that is simple to state and has real consequences for how targets are drugged.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and the structural basis of degraders. Handa, Ito and others have a strong claim for the thalidomide-cereblon molecular glue mechanism, so the three-person limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but approvals are still limited. Mechanistic understanding is solid, yet the timing may be somewhat early for full clinical verdict.
uncertainties: Allocation between the PROTAC and molecular glue strands is unresolved.
Late-stage clinical outcomes remain uncertain; my recollection of the trial status may be out of date.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs for site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids made it possible to design proteins with new chemistry in living cells. It is a clean, original idea that is broadly used in enzymology, biophysics and protein therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended to multi-site and quadruplet codon reprogramming and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama have genuine claims, but the three above best capture priority and breadth.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of independent confirmation and widespread applications. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Schultz, Wang and Chin may be argued differently.
Overlap with earlier Nobel work on directed evolution and phage display is modest but present.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnel picture of protein folding explained how a random chain finds its native state and unified theory with experiment, in the spirit of quantitative theory tied to measurement. It has shaped how the field thinks about folding, misfolding and design, and fed into structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are central to the funnel theory; Fersht's phi-value analysis provides the experimental mapping. Bryngelson and Dill have strong claims, so credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are well established and widely confirmed; recognition is arguably late, though 2024 recognition of structure prediction may shift how the committee sees the field.
uncertainties: The weighting between theory and experiment contributors is uncertain.
Whether 2024 is considered to have already covered the folding theme is a concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled siRNA and mRNA medicines, including the COVID-19 vaccines. This is a plainly game-changing delivery technology with demonstrated global consequences, and the chemistry of pKa-tuned lipids and self-assembly is central.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues at UBC (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the lipid nanoparticle systems; Langer and Anderson contributed lipid libraries and delivery materials. Attribution is the main obstacle because many people contributed and the three-person limit is tight.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at enormous scale, so very mature. The 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification, not the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Fair split between UBC lipid pioneers and the MIT delivery school is unclear.
Patent and priority disputes may complicate the record; I cannot verify details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on DNA without double-strand breaks, a simple and elegant use of deaminase chemistry that has opened therapeutic routes now in the clinic. A clear follow-on from the 2020 CRISPR prize but distinct.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental work; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors on the cytosine and adenine editors respectively. Kondo and Nishida independently reported a deaminase-based editor, so priority is not entirely clean.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is early but proof of concept is strong. Slightly early for a prize, and the 2020 award may make the committee cautious about another CRISPR-derived prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants another genome-editing prize so soon.
Role of Kondo and Nishida in priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned potentials give near quantum accuracy at force-field cost, enabling simulations of reactions and materials at scales previously unreachable. It is a major methodological change, close to my own field, though I should be careful about favouring my own area.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's neural network potentials and Bartók and Csányi's Gaussian approximation potentials are the pillars; the many-contributor field makes a clean three-person split difficult.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly evolving, with growing independent validation but unresolved questions about transferability and long-range physics. Probably early.
uncertainties: Generalisation and reliability across chemistry are not settled.
Credit is spread over several groups and recent foundation models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle for cellular compartments is a new concept with wide consequences for biochemistry and disease, linking physical chemistry to cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne reported P granule condensates in 2009; Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase separation. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical-chemistry frameworks; the choice among them is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely accepted, but physiological roles and some interpretations are debated. Timing is plausible but not fully mature.
uncertainties: Debate over physiological relevance versus in vitro artefacts.
Whether the topic is seen as chemistry rather than cell biology.
